title: Choose ConceptStudio's visual world
question: The roll assigned The Instant Print. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: The Instant Print
options.lineage: instant-film prints and the albums they live in
options.thesis: Every training example is a print, and its caption is written in the print's wide bottom margin.
options.viewport: Review as a charcoal shell around one large print: the photo above, NORA7 set large at the start of the margin, the editable caption below it, the other prints as a strip.
options.risk: Can tip into nostalgia or scrapbook cuteness if the margin turns handwritten or the prints tilt.

raised.raise: Nothing disappears, it cancels: final, edited and excluded states stamp themselves onto the print margin, and excluded prints stay visible, struck through.
Photography is never tinted or filtered by the interface, and one typeface carries both the large trigger and the caption.
Only the print under review carries the accent ring; every other print stays neutral.
Hierarchy by scale contrast: the trigger word at display size on the print, every other label small.

options.label: The Field Guide
options.lineage: naturalist field guides and their identification plates
options.thesis: Teaching a model a concept is identifying a species: field marks hold the concept, habitat notes describe the rest.
options.viewport: Review as a plate: the photo with leader lines from the concept's field marks to NORA7, the caption below as the habitat note, the other samples as numbered plates.
options.risk: The most familiar reading of annotation, close to the cat icon draft, and its callouts echo the portfolio's locator bubbles.

options.label: Terminal Wayfinding
options.thesis: The nine steps as a signed concourse: one band always shows the next action and what it costs.
options.viewport: Review with a yellow band across the top: 3 captions left to check, next: Publish, and the photo and caption below in a quiet working area.
options.case: Holds product clarity, since one obvious next action is a product principle; loses audience identification, because people training a likeness do not live in airports.
options.risk: Saturated yellow everywhere turns into a costume; yellow must stay reserved for the next-action band.

options.label: One Frame at a Time
options.thesis: Review as a feed of one: the sample owns the canvas, its caption anchored low, the next one a keystroke away.
options.viewport: Review with the photo filling the work area, the editable caption over a soft scrim at the bottom, a rail of final, re-caption and exclude on the right.
options.case: Holds audience identification, since everyone knows the gesture; clarity is strong on Review but weaker on the money and settings screens.
options.risk: Dark and immersive can read as a consumer feed or an expert tool, both of which the brief rules out.

options.label: Ticket Wallet
options.thesis: The journey as a coupon book that always shows what remains.
options.viewport: Each step a coupon, torn off when done.
options.case: Fuses on the journey but not on the photo-and-caption task, and the audience does not identify with it.
options.risk: Nostalgic paper costume on a working screen.

options.label: Design Annual Plates
options.thesis: Every sample a credited plate on near-white stock.
options.viewport: Samples as plates with credit rows for captions.
options.case: Reads to designers, not to beginners, and its crosshairs and hairlines sit too close to the portfolio's drawing set.
options.risk: A costume of the owner's own site.
options.kept: Untinted photography; one typeface for display and caption alike.

options.label: Star Atlas
options.thesis: The dataset as a sky of ranked points.
options.viewport: Samples plotted as stars sized by quality.
options.case: Neither carries the photo-and-caption task nor reads to the audience.
options.risk: Decoration over a task that is about one photo and its words.
options.kept: The object under the eye is ringed in one colour; everything else stays chalk.

options.label: Type Specimen
options.thesis: The trigger as a specimen word at enormous scale.
options.viewport: NORA7 at display size over a grid of samples.
options.case: Type-world identity with no hold on photos, captions or money.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A first-class native Mac photo tool, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Review as sidebar, sample grid and an inspector holding the caption, the way Photos and Lightroom arrange it.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other Mac utility by design.
